summary: On-demand immutable audit batch with tamper-evident index for third-party incident responder
description: Issue summary: Customer requests a one-time, on-demand delivery of a tamper-evident, immutable audit export covering a 72-hour incident window (2026-02-10 03:00 UTC to 2026-02-13 03:00 UTC). The package must be suitable for handoff to an external incident response vendor and include: a canonicalized newline-delimited JSON export, SHA-256 manifests for each file, a signed index file (timestamped and KMS-attested), and a short verification guide. Impact: Customer needs this for an ongoing third-party incident response and regulator notification. They cannot proceed with containment and reporting without a verifiable audit bundle. Environment: prod/us-east (multi-tenant org with four sub-tenants). Requested format: NDJSON (UTF-8), UTC timestamps canonicalized to RFC3339, per-record event IDs retained, and per-tenant envelope. Delivery method: Pre-signed S3 objects in a customer-provided bucket (they will provide a cross-account role), plus an additional gzip-compressed tarball signed with Redwood's code-signing key. Security requirements: do not include full message payloads for events flagged PII-SENSITIVE; instead include a redaction manifest showing which fields were removed and a reversible pseudonymization map accessible only to Peregrine under an HMAC-wrapped envelope. Steps to reproduce / produce request: 1) Customer asked through account team with incident reference PEREG-IR-2026-02; 2) Support to validate retention window and tenant scoping; 3) Support to coordinate with SRE/archiving to generate export and KMS-signed index. Logs / evidence already provided by customer: screenshot of incident timeline, tenant IDs, and the cross-account role ARN. Deliverables checklist requested: per-file SHA-256, signed index, gzipped tarball, redaction manifest, chain-of-custody notes, and instructions for local verification.

investigation_notes: Initial export: audit-service supports per-tenant NDJSON exports and computes per-file SHA-256. Packaging step used gzip --rsyncable leading to slight variance in binary layout that caused mismatch with vendor's local checksum that expected raw NDJSON checksum.
Root cause: packaging pipeline included an extra newline on shard boundary when compressing; canonicalization step was incomplete for multi-shard outputs.

Mitigation applied: forced canonicalization to RFC3339 timestamps, normalized newline handling (LF only), regenerated NDJSON shards, recomputed SHA-256 on raw NDJSON before compression, and signed index references to raw-object checksums.
Security review: HSM-wrapped reversible pseudonymization map acceptable for short retention; we will store the HMAC key material under Redwood KMS and create an attested deletion workflow.
resolution_notes: Export regenerated and verified. Re-delivered gzipped tarball and separate per-tenant NDJSON files to customer-provided S3 bucket using their cross-account role with SSE-KMS enabled.
Signed index file created and timestamped using projects/redwood/kms/keys/audit-signing. Index contains SHA-256 of raw NDJSON shards (pre-compression).
Chain-of-custody artifact added: packaging job ID, SRE operator, timestamps for generation, packaging, signing, and delivery.
